capabilities.title: Fatigue and durability
capabilities.description: Investigate behaviour under repeated loading, characterise fatigue response and compare life predictions with experimental results.

capabilities.title: Mechanical characterisation
capabilities.description: Study the mechanical response of engineering materials and components. Previous research includes polymer composites, hybrid joints and the influence of temperature on material behaviour.

capabilities.title: Joints and structural integrity
capabilities.description: Connect measurements and computational analysis to assess welded components and mechanical joints, including residual stresses and fatigue response.

capabilities.title: Numerical–experimental validation
capabilities.description: Combine finite element analysis with mechanical measurements to examine model predictions. Research experience includes strain, vibration and temperature measurements and component-level correlation.

capabilities.title: Engineering data and methods
capabilities.description: Process experimental data, develop scientific software and compare analytical or computational methods. Reproducible datasets and documented algorithms support interpretation and model validation.

measurement_context.title: Material and joint response
measurement_context.description: Previous studies document static and fatigue characterisation of materials and joints. The specimen, loading conditions and required measurements define the feasibility of a new campaign.

measurement_context.title: Strain, vibration and temperature
measurement_context.description: These measurement categories feature in existing research. Sensors, acquisition settings, operating ranges and facility access must be confirmed for each investigation.

measurement_context.title: Model correlation and data processing
measurement_context.description: Experimental results can be compared with finite element and analytical models, using scientific programming to evaluate predictions and document the analysis.

equipment.title: StepLab electrodynamic axial–torsional system
equipment.description: Combined axial and torsional fatigue loading; maximum frequency depends on the operating mode and specimen. Round specimens Ø 6–12 mm and flat specimens up to 15 mm thick.
equipment.image_alt: StepLab experimental testing system with guarded frame
equipment.image_caption: StepLab experimental testing equipment. The photograph is not used to identify the rated machine model.

equipment.title: Schenck servo-hydraulic axial–torsional system
equipment.description: Combined tension/compression and torsion with an internal-pressure actuator rated to 700 bar for tubular specimens. Historical group documentation reports approximately 10–20 Hz. Round grips Ø 5–40 mm; flat grips 8–20 mm thick. Limits depend on the test setup and are not necessarily simultaneous.
equipment.image_alt: Hydraulic actuators and fixture of experimental testing system
equipment.image_caption: Hydraulic test setup; precise actuator identity to be confirmed against the machine register.

equipment.title: Rumul resonant fatigue-testing systems
equipment.description: The group's historical facilities inventory lists two resonant machines rated 20 kN and 150 kN, with typical operating frequencies of 100–150 Hz. Resonant loading and crack-growth studies depend on specimen geometry and controller configuration. The photograph is not linked to either stated capacity.
equipment.image_alt: Green Rumul resonant fatigue-testing machine with grips and load frame
equipment.image_caption: Rumul resonant machine; the specific capacity of the pictured unit is not asserted.

equipment.title: MTS uniaxial servo-hydraulic systems
equipment.description: The historical laboratory inventory reports two uniaxial testing systems, rated 25 kN and 100 kN, with frequencies typically up to 10–20 Hz. Their present availability is subject to verification.

equipment.title: StepLab electromechanical testing system
equipment.description: A smaller electromechanical machine for compatible specimens and operating modes; model-specific photograph not yet confirmed.

equipment.title: Reconfigurable structural testing bench
equipment.description: A configurable test bench with three Schenck hydraulic actuators supports research-specific setups for welded joints, structural components and vehicle frames. The older facilities page separately describes a bench with up to seven hydraulic actuators; this historical rating is not presented as the current configuration.
equipment.image_alt: Large modular steel test bench with tiled loading surface
equipment.image_caption: Reconfigurable structural testing bench in the Machine Design laboratory.

equipment.title: Vibration and modal investigations
equipment.description: Experiment-specific shaker and instrumentation arrangements support structural-dynamics measurements. The historical group inventory also describes a robotic vibrometry setup. Operating ranges depend on the actual equipment and configuration.
equipment.image_alt: Electrodynamic shaker beneath mechanical component during experimental testing

equipment.title: Thermal and environmental conditioning
equipment.description: An induction oven supports temperatures up to 900 °C, a resistance oven operates between 200 and 1000 °C, and one climatic chamber for compatible StepLab arrangements operates from −30 to +180 °C. Combined availability depends on individual systems.

equipment.title: Specimen production and metrology
equipment.description: In-house CNC turning, milling, and conventional tooling for round, flat, notched and tubular specimens. Surface roughness measurement (Ra/Rz) and Vickers hardness testing support material characterisation.

equipment.title: FLIR X6901sc infrared thermography
equipment.description: High-speed cooled InSb infrared camera for experimental thermal measurements. Values are manufacturer's instrument specifications; actual calibration, optics, filters and acquisition configuration must be checked for each investigation.
equipment.image_caption: FLIR X6901sc camera; acquisition parameters depend on the configuration.
